# `fluxsim story`

Tell the history of one row of a committed run: the rows that link to it and the rows it links to, through the relationships the run's contract declares, a few hops out, ordered by their first date or timestamp column. Each stream is checked against the receipt's outputDigest before it is read, and nothing is written. Every row of the expose that matches --key is the entity, and its rows come first. A first line says how many rows matched. Then one line per row: its date, its expose, its key, its hop (0 for the entity's own rows, n for a row reached after n relationships), the relationship it was reached by (- at hop 0), then column=value pairs, with control characters written out. With --json, a story is one JSON object per row, with hop and relationship, and no envelope; a refusal is the usual JSON envelope.

## Synopsis

```text
fluxsim story [options]
```

## Examples

```bash
# the rows that link to customer 42 and the rows it links to, two hops out
fluxsim story --run-id de72fa4b22711c52 --emit customer --key 42

# one row of a composite key and its direct neighbours, one JSON object per line
fluxsim story --run-id de72fa4b22711c52 --emit store_returns \
    --key sr_item_sk=7 --key sr_ticket_number=1001 --depth 1 --json
```

## Options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--run-id` | `RUN_ID` | the run id to act on (as reported by `fluxsim plan`/`fluxsim run`) **(required)** |
| `--emit` | `EXPOSE` | the expose whose row is the entity, by its exposeId **(required)** |
| `--key` | `VALUE|COLUMN=VALUE` | the entity's key, compared as the canonical text of the column's value: one VALUE for the expose's one-column key, or COLUMN=VALUE once per column of a composite key **(required)** |
| `--depth` | `N` | how many links away from the entity the story reaches (default: 2) |
| `--limit` | `N` | the most rows the story keeps, nearest the entity first; says when it cut (default: 200) |
| `--state-dir` | `STATE_DIR` | run-state directory (default: ./.flux) |
| `-j, --json` |  | emit machine-readable JSON |
